title: Nick Drake: The Artist
description: Three albums, barely noticed in his lifetime, now treasured: the life, the records and the people behind Nick Drake's quiet music.

cards.prompt: Nick Drake was a singer-songwriter from which country?
cards.details: His music is often described as quintessentially English: pastoral, misty and understated.

cards.prompt: Nick Drake was born in 1948 in Rangoon, in which country?
cards.details: His father worked there as an engineer. The family moved back to England when Nick was a small child.

cards.prompt: In which Warwickshire village did Nick Drake grow up?
cards.details: The family home, Far Leys, is where he made many home recordings, and where he spent his final years.

cards.prompt: Which university did Nick Drake attend (and leave before graduating)?
cards.details: He studied English literature there, but left to focus on music before finishing his degree.

cards.prompt: How many studio albums did Nick Drake release in his lifetime?
cards.details: All three sold poorly at the time. Their reputation grew enormously after his death.

cards.prompt: What is Nick Drake's 1969 debut album?
cards.details: Gentle guitar and voice wrapped in beautiful string arrangements.

cards.prompt: The title Five Leaves Left comes from a warning printed in packets of what?
cards.details: Near the end of a packet of rolling papers, a slip warned that only five leaves were left.

cards.prompt: Which friend from Cambridge wrote the string arrangements on Five Leaves Left?
cards.details: His lush, sympathetic strings are a big part of why the album sounds so timeless.

cards.prompt: Which Five Leaves Left song, with a hypnotic string arrangement, is often named among his finest?
cards.details: Unusually for Drake, its strings were arranged by Harry Robinson rather than Robert Kirby.

cards.prompt: Which American-born producer signed Nick Drake and produced his first two albums?
cards.details: Boyd also produced Fairport Convention and the Incredible String Band, and was a champion of Drake's music.

cards.prompt: On which record label were all three of Nick Drake's albums released?
cards.details: Island was the home of much of the British folk-rock scene at the time.

cards.prompt: What is Nick Drake's second album, with full-band arrangements?
cards.details: His most "produced" record, with a full band, brass and strings. The title is a twist on "brighter later".

cards.prompt: Which former Velvet Underground member played on Bryter Layter?
cards.details: Cale added piano, celeste and more, most famously on "Northern Sky".

cards.prompt: Which Bryter Layter song, featuring John Cale, is often called one of the most beautiful love songs ever written?
cards.details: One of the rare moments of pure joy in his catalogue.

cards.prompt: Bryter Layter has two songs sharing which name, numbered I and II?
cards.details: Confusingly, "Hazey Jane II" comes before "Hazey Jane I" on the album.

cards.prompt: What is Nick Drake's third and final album?
cards.details: Stark and short: just voice and guitar. See the Pink Moon set for the full story.

cards.prompt: Drake was known for playing guitar in unusual what?
cards.details: He re-tuned his guitar for many songs, which is partly why his intricate parts are so hard to copy.

cards.prompt: Nick Drake's older sister became a well-known actress. What is her name?
cards.details: She later helped look after his musical legacy.

cards.prompt: In what year did Nick Drake die, aged 26?
cards.details: He died at home of an overdose of antidepressants. He had struggled with depression for years.

cards.prompt: A 2000 TV advert for which car brand introduced Nick Drake to a huge new audience?
cards.details: The ad used "Pink Moon", and his record sales jumped dramatically, decades after his death.
